title: Hennings marketing project
titleCn: Hennings软饮料公司营销项目讨论

paragraphs.text: Part three. You will hear two business students called Sue and Gary discussing their plan for a marketing project. First, you have some time to look at questions twenty-one to twenty-four.
Now listen carefully and answer questions twenty-one to twenty-four.
Hello Sue. Sorry I'm a bit late.
Hi, Gary.
We've got to plan our marketing project, haven't we? But I missed the last lecture, so can you remind me exactly what we've got to do?
We're looking at Hennings, the soft drinks manufacturer. We've got to think of a new product that the company could offer and then design the first stages of a marketing campaign.
What kind of drink does it have to be?
That's up to us.
Then what about some kind of health drink?
Fine by me, but then I think we should decide exactly who we want to sell it to, because that'll probably affect everything else. Sporty men, younger women.
Children. That'll be more fun to market. So this is week one we're in now, so we've got that sorted, and we've got seven weeks altogether.
What should we do in week two then?
I think we should spend that week doing desk research, you know, gathering as much information as possible from newspapers and the Internet.
Oh, good idea. We'll need information before we make any other decisions.
Okay, I've written that in.
Shall we divide the areas we're going to study? I could look at some trade figures, you know. I'll get the ones which are most up to date.
Do you think that'll be useful?
I think we need to know something about other products like this and their performance.
Okay, sounds a good idea. You do that, and meanwhile, I could have a good look at some of the websites of Henning's competitors to see what kind of products they offer and what their plans are.
Okay, got that.
Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions twenty-five to thirty.
Now listen and answer questions twenty-five to thirty.
What next?
I think sometime in week three we should meet up and pool our information.
Yes, and then one of us should actually write it up. Then we'll have section one of the report done.
We could do that later, couldn't we?
I think it's better to do it straight away while it's fresh in our minds. I'll volunteer for that. I don't mind.
Okay. Thanks, Gary. I've noted that. Next, week four.
We'll need to write a product description, you know, a detailed one to use in the market survey. Shall I do that too?
Okay. And the following week I could be designing a questionnaire for store managers to send out with it.
Questionnaires are tricky to write, aren't they? I've got a book that might be useful if you want to borrow it.
Oh, have you?
Yes. It's got a checklist that's very helpful.
Great. I'm making a note of that on the plan. Okay. And that's it, isn't it?
Not quite. Don't you remember the lecturer said we should include a media plan for the advertising campaign?
Okay. So we'll use week six to produce that. Then that gives us just one week to finalize the report. Is that okay?
It's fine. We'll have drafted most of it anyway as we go along.
That is the end of part three. You now have one minute to check your answers to part three.
